This means that even for crash halts, the system can cheaply identify and excise the partial write, then resume from the verified prefix—provided the storage layer can identify which physical writes belong to which MMR peak.

Under this regime, the distinction between budget halts and crash halts vanishes—both are resumable if the storage layer's atomicity guarantee holds, and resumption must be refused only when the storage guarantee itself is violated (disk failure, corruption, Byzantine storage nodes).
survivors.mechanism: The storage layer exposes an atomic append operation: append(event) returns success only after the event is durably persisted and fsync'd, or returns failure if the operation did not complete. The reasoning system calls append for each event and checks the return. Budget exhaustion is checked after append returns—never during. A crash during append leaves either a fully written event or nothing, by the storage layer's guarantee. On resumption, the system reads the log tail and verifies the last event is complete (its declared length matches its actual bytes, and its hash is valid). If so, resumption proceeds; if the storage guarantee was violated (e.g., fsync was not honored, or a partial sector was written), the tail event will fail validation and resumption is refused.
